questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How chefs make food look good on the plate
Why some kinds of music are bad for digestion
How sounds affect taste and what we buy
Famous chocolate adverts on British TV
questions.why: Beth says they'll investigate the link between sound and our tastebuds, called 'sonic seasoning'.

options: Using sounds or music to boost flavours
Adding salt to food in time with music
Cooking food quickly with sound waves
Making food crunchier and louder to eat
questions.why: Beth says it's the idea that certain sounds or music can enhance flavours in food.

options: To show that chocolate tastes better quietly
To give an example of music used to sell food
To explain how chocolate is made in factories
To compare the taste of chocolate and whisky
questions.why: He says food companies know sounds equal sales, and Cadbury hired an orchestra to represent its flavours.

questions.q: What does Professor Charles Spence think about sound and taste?
options: Sound is less important than sight and smell
Sound only matters after we start eating
Sound has no real effect on taste
Sound is more important than we realise
questions.why: He says, 'I think it's much more important than we realise'.

questions.q: According to Professor Spence, what do sounds like a sizzling steak do?
options: They make us expect a certain taste
They make us less hungry
They warn us the food is too hot
They make the food cook faster
questions.why: He says these sounds are cues that set up expectations about what we're about to taste.

questions.q: Who chooses the music at the Smashburger restaurant?
options: The customers
The chefs
Professional music pickers
Professor Spence
questions.why: Every song is specially chosen by professional music pickers.

questions.q: According to Amy Frishkey, how can good music affect customers?
options: It makes them eat faster and leave early
It makes them order less food and drink
It helps them concentrate on their talk
It can lead them to buy extras, like dessert
questions.why: She says music can put you in a mood that leads to an impulse buy, like dessert.

questions.q: What does Neil suggest restaurants gain from customers staying longer?
options: More time to clean
More money
Better reviews online
Quieter dining rooms
questions.why: He says the longer customers linger and buy on impulse, the more money a restaurant makes.
